title: Kingdom of Kongo
summary: The Kingdom of Kongo arose in the late fourteenth century from an alliance of principalities south of the lower Congo River, ruled from its capital Mbanza Kongo. Its kings adopted Christianity under Afonso I (r. 1506-1543) after missionaries arrived in 1491. Defeat at Mbwila in 1665 and civil wars left it largely disintegrated as an independent state by 1710.

uncertainty.note: Start "late 14th century" (World History Encyclopedia) is shown as c. 1390 for placement only. UNESCO gives the 14th to 19th centuries for the kingdom as a whole; the king title continued after 1710, which is the date it had "all but disintegrated" as an independent state.

importance.justification: One of the largest states of western central Africa and the first sub-Saharan kingdom to adopt Christianity as a state religion; a centre of the Atlantic slave trade route.

related.because: UNESCO says the kingdom lay at the centre of the most important route for the trade in enslaved people.
